label: ASSUMPTION (proposed by qwen3:4b; not evidence)
value_proposition: Get important Slack messages without missing them when you're not looking at the channel.
current_alternatives: Using Slack's built-in search to find missed messages
Third-party Slack apps that summarize threads

channels.name: r/remoteengineering
channels.why: Active community of remote engineers who use Slack daily and have experienced message overload

channels.name: Slack Dev Community
channels.why: Dedicated Slack ecosystem users who discuss tooling and workflow improvements

channels.name: Product Manager Slack
channels.why: Specialized group for product managers on distributed teams who face similar communication challenges

key_metric: Time spent reviewing missed Slack messages per week
pricing_rationale: Anchor to the cost of manual message scanning in Slack (5 EUR) and third-party Slack apps (10-20 EUR) that users currently pay for
interview_questions: Tell me about the last time you missed an important Slack message and had to go back through the thread to find it?
How much time did you spend reviewing Slack messages you missed last week?
What did you do when you realized you missed a Slack message?
How often do you check Slack messages outside of work hours?
What tools do you use to track missed Slack messages?
launch_angle: Focus on reducing time spent reviewing missed Slack messages for remote engineers and product managers
riskiest_assumption: Remote engineers and product managers spend significant time reviewing missed Slack messages
kill_criterion: Stop if fewer than 3 of 10 interviewees reported spending more than 30 minutes per week reviewing missed Slack messages
